thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — tomorrow 09:30 UTC we’ll do a live runthrough of the eu-west4 GPU cluster bring-up and the official on-call handoff.

maria: Goal is to validate bootstrap, paging configs, ownership, and run escalation scenarios so the on-call rotation is comfortable. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eu-west4-provisioning (please don’t share externally).

drew: I’ll lead the provisioning steps and show the terraform -> image bake -> nodepool create flow. Plan: ~20m provisioning, 10m health checks, 15m simulated incidents.

kai: Can we also test the PagerDuty mappings? Last time the severities were flipped and it woke the wrong tier.

maria: Yes — we’ll test PD service: "eu-west4-gpu-cluster" and mappings: P0 -> SRE primary, P1 -> SRE secondary, P2 -> infra rotation. I updated the routing rules in PD (see the runbook section "Paging and Escalation").

sylvia: I’ll be there to validate ML image compatibility and GPU visibility (NVIDIA drivers, cuda, container runtime). I’ll run the quick check list:
- nvidia-smi inside pod
- /dev/nvidia* nodes visible
- GPU utilization metrics on metrics.redwood

tom: For on-call training, can we run the following scenarios?
1) Single-node GPU OOM -> autoscaler doesn’t add capacity
2) CNI flaps causing pod-network unavailable
3) Image pull failures for pre-baked images

maria: Yep. We’ll inject 1) by draining a node and simulating workload spike; 2) by toggling vpc-subnet route (infra-bot will simulate); 3) by pointing an image tag to a non-existent manifest.

infra-bot: reminder: scheduled maintenance window available 2026-03-19T09:30Z -> will annotate alerts as "test" while runthrough in progress. Use command: `infra-bot annotate --run eu-west4-provisioning --tag test-run`

drew: Checklist snippet I’ll walk through (copied to channel so folks can rehearse locally):
```
# minimal validation steps
terraform apply -var=region=eu-west4
./bake-image.sh --base ami-ml-2026 --cuda 12
kubectl apply -f nodepool-eu-west4.yaml
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node -l pool=gpu --timeout=10m
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu
```

kai: Good. For paging thresholds — suggest: node_not_ready for 3m -> P1, control_plane_unhealthy for 1m -> P0, GPU_util_spike >90% for 10m -> P2 (investigate cost/denial). Anyone object?

sylvia: Fine by me. Also add an alert for "image_pullbackoff" aggregated across 3+ nodes -> P1.

maria: Escalation path in runbook: SRE primary -> 15m -> SRE secondary -> 15m -> infra on-call -> 30m -> Eng-triage pager. Also included paging docs for on-call transfer (how to hand ownership in PD).

tom: For the transfer itself, what does "ownership" include? (I’ll take first week after bake)

maria: Ownership = initial triage, runbook follow, maintain the pinned incident doc in confluence, and own the PD schedule for that service. Also: verify cost alarms and usage tags daily for the first 3 days (we’ve seen runaway training jobs).

drew: Cost controls we’ll enable: billed-ops alert at $4000/day for the cluster, and quota soft limits per project. Also enforce tags: team, env, owner. I’ll add a quick command to list untagged instances in the runbook.

sylvia: Training note: show new on-call how to run the cheap smoke test for models: deploy a small container with test load, confirm latencies < 200ms for init tokens.

maria: Last bits — please join the dry-run 09:30 UTC. Bring a laptop. If you can’t make it, ping me and we’ll record the session. After the runthrough I’ll flip ownership in PagerDuty and post the screenshot of the mapping here.

kai: I’ll be there. One more ask: can someone dump the kube-proxy and CNI logs easily for the runbook? I’ll add quick grep commands to the runbook.

drew: yep — I added these snippets under "Diagnostics":
```
kubectl -n kube-system logs -l k8s-app=kube-proxy --tail=200
kubectl -n kube-system logs -l k8s-app=calico-node --tail=200
```

infra-bot: note: object storage bucket eu-west4-cluster-logs will be writable by oncall group during test window. Use `gsutil cp` to upload artifacts.

maria: Great — plan acknowledged. I’ll post the meeting invite + Zoom and attach the final checklist by EOD. :white_check_mark: 

kai: Thanks — makes the handoff feel less scary :slightly_smiling_face:

sylvia: Thanks all, see you tomorrow.

maria: (recording will be posted)"
